subject.title: fix(agents): distinguish terminal aborts from retryable failures (#60388)

question: Should OpenClaw treat run-budget, cron timeout-string, HTTP client-disconnect, and marked `abortable()` wrapper aborts as terminal so they skip provider fallback and profile rotation?
rationale: The implementation looks technically sound, but it deliberately changes fallback/provider behavior for existing configurations, so a maintainer needs to own the terminal-versus-retryable policy boundary.

options.title: Accept Terminal-Abort Boundary
options.body: Merge after the fallback/provider owner confirms these OpenClaw-owned aborts should stop fallback across run-budget, cron, compaction, and HTTP disconnect paths.

options.title: Narrow Sources Before Merge
options.body: Limit the branch to the embedded private-controller run-budget path and leave cron strings or HTTP disconnect tagging to separate decisions.

options.title: Pause For Budgeted Fallback Design
options.body: Hold or close this branch if maintainers prefer a remaining-budget fallback design over terminal aborts overriding configured fallbacks.

recommendation.title: Accept Terminal-Abort Boundary
recommendation.body: Merge after the fallback/provider owner confirms these OpenClaw-owned aborts should stop fallback across run-budget, cron, compaction, and HTTP disconnect paths.

likelyOwner.reason: altaywtf is assigned, supplied the live provider proof, and is already engaged on the provider-side abort boundary for this PR.
